construct: Type II pneumocytes synthesize and secrete pulmonary surfactant, a phospholipid-rich mixture whose major phospholipid is dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine (DPPC). Surfactant lowers surface tension at the alveolar air-liquid interface, stabilizes small alveoli during expiration, and increases lung compliance. Premature infants may have inadequate surfactant and develop diffuse atelectasis and respiratory distress.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A 29-week infant with early diffuse neonatal RDS has inadequate type-II-pneumocyte surfactant; the major surface-active phospholipid DPPC lowers alveolar surface tension and prevents end-expiratory collapse.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Elastin affects elastic recoil and can influence lung mechanics, but it is not the alveolar lining component whose deficiency raises air-liquid surface tension in premature RDS.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Prematurity, early RDS, reduced compliance, and alveolar collapse uniquely identify deficient DPPC-rich surfactant.
